input.doc_title: Graph-Aware Prompting for Reliable Section Generation
input.doc_summary: We present a graph-guided prompting workflow for long-form scientific writing that prioritizes evidence and citation consistency. Our method constructs a document graph that encodes section dependencies and uses strict JSON schemas and evidence-aware prompts to generate and validate individual sections. At generation time, the system (1) builds a section graph and schedules leaf-first writing, (2) retrieves and injects relevant evidence for each section, (3) produces JSON-constrained section outputs, and (4) assembles a LaTeX manuscript with refs.bib. We evaluate the approach by comparing it to a baseline linear prompting pipeline on two topical domains, measuring citation coverage, hallucination rate, and reviewer-style scores. Results show improved citation coverage and reduced unsupported assertions while keeping edits and post-hoc audits straightforward via machine-readable outputs. We intentionally state conservative claims and require explicit source citations for all factual assertions. The paper contributes practical artifacts: a graph-based section scheduler, an evidence-injection protocol per section, and an audit-friendly JSON output format that integrates with standard LaTeX/bib workflows. Our experiments use internal notes and a small curated PDF set where available; metrics focus on citation fidelity and factual consistency rather than broad generalization.
input.target_audience: ACL Workshop on Natural Language Generation
input.parent_summary: Describe experimental setup: two topical domains, baseline linear prompting comparator, datasets (internal notes and a small curated PDF set if available), and evaluation protocol. Specify metrics: citation coverage, hallucination rate (unsupported assertions), and reviewer score.

output.title: Experimental domains and datasets
output.summary: Specify the two topical domains used for evaluation and justify their selection. Describe the datasets per domain: internal author notes and, where available, a small curated set of PDFs. Document dataset composition (number of source documents per domain if available), preprocessing steps, any train/validation/test splits or leave-one-out protocol, and privacy or access constraints that affect reproducibility.

output.title: Baselines and system configuration
output.summary: Detail the baseline linear prompting comparator and the graph-aware prompting system variants evaluated. List implementation details to report (model family or API used, prompt templates, JSON schema enforcement, evidence-retrieval mechanism, and key generation hyperparameters). State any ablations or alternate schedules compared and note computational budget and randomness controls (e.g., seeds) insofar as space permits.

output.title: Evaluation protocol and metrics
output.summary: Define the evaluation workflow: how sections are sampled or aggregated, human reviewer procedures for reviewer-style scores, and automated audits. Precisely define metrics: citation coverage, hallucination rate (unsupported assertions per section), and reviewer scoring rubric. Explain how citation coverage and unsupported assertions are measured (e.g., presence/absence of explicit source citations tied to assertions), any inter-annotator agreement checks, and the statistical comparisons or tests used to compare systems.
